claim: Hippocampome.org is a comprehensive knowledge base of neuron types in the rodent hippocampal formation (dentate gyrus, CA3, CA2, CA1, subiculum, and entorhinal cortex).
source: Hippocampome.org is a comprehensive knowledge base of neuron types in the rodent hippocampal formation (dentate gyrus, CA3, CA2, CA1, subiculum, and entorhinal cortex).
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract as a description of the resource.

claim: The extensive literature mining and data reconciliation identified 122 neuron types based on neurotransmitter, axonal and dendritic patterns, synaptic specificity, electrophysiology, and molecular biomarkers.
source: Our extensive literature mining and data reconciliation identified 122 neuron types based on neurotransmitter, axonal and dendritic patterns, synaptic specificity, electrophysiology, and molecular biomarkers.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract as a result of the literature mining effort.

claim: All ∼3700 annotated properties are individually supported by specific evidence (∼14,000 pieces) in peer-reviewed publications.
source: All ∼3700 annotated properties are individually supported by specific evidence (∼14,000 pieces) in peer-reviewed publications.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a quantification of the knowledge base content.

claim: The rodent hippocampus is among the most intensively studied neural systems.
source: As a case in point, the rodent hippocampus is among the most intensively studied neural systems.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established knowledge about the hippocampus.

claim: Numerous seminal efforts have summarized the enormous amount of information on the morphology, connectivity, biochemistry, and electrophysiology of hippocampal neurons.
source: Numerous seminal efforts have summarized the enormous amount of information on the morphology, connectivity, biochemistry, and electrophysiology of hippocampal neurons (Bernard and Wheal, 1994; Patton and McNaughton, 1995; Freund and Buzsáki, 1996; Parra et al., 1998; McBain and Fisahn, 2001; Maccaferri and Lacaille, 2003; Amaral and Lavenex, 2007; Canto et al., 2008; Klausberger and Somogyi, 2008; Klausberger, 2009; Somogyi, 2010; Bezaire and Soltesz, 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to review articles.

claim: The hippocampus plays a critical role in the consolidation and retrieval of episodic memory.
source: The hippocampus plays a critical role in the consolidation and retrieval of episodic memory (Nadel and Moscovitch, 1997; Wang and Morris, 2010) as well as in spatial representation and navigation (Foster and Knierim, 2012; Moser et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research.

claim: The hippocampus plays a critical role in spatial representation and navigation.
source: The hippocampus plays a critical role in the consolidation and retrieval of episodic memory (Nadel and Moscovitch, 1997; Wang and Morris, 2010) as well as in spatial representation and navigation (Foster and Knierim, 2012; Moser et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published research.

claim: The hippocampal formation is commonly delineated into 26 cytoarchitectural parcels.
source: The orderly anatomical organization of the hippocampal formation is commonly delineated into 26 cytoarchitectural parcels (Figure 1A,B): DG outer stratum (s.) moleculare (SMo), inner s. moleculare (SMi), s. granulosum (SG), hilus (H); CA3 s. lacunosum-moleculare (SLM), s. radiatum (SR), s. lucidum (SL), s. pyramidale (SP), s. oriens (SO); 4 each in CA2 and CA1 (same as CA3 except SL); Sub s. moleculare (SM), SP, polymorphic layer (PL); and EC layers I–VI.
evidence: Stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A,B.

claim: The binary representation (present or not) of both axons and dendrites across the 26 hippocampal parcels is sufficient to identify >100 unique morphological profiles based on existing literature.
source: Specifically, the binary representation (present or not) of both axons and dendrites across the 26 hippocampal parcels (see 'Materials and methods') is sufficient to identify >100 unique morphological profiles based on existing literature (selection in Figure 1F; complete data: hippocampome.org/morphology).
evidence: Stated in the text and supported by Figure 1F showing morphological patterns.

claim: A key assumption of this framework is that neurons differing in axonal or dendritic patterns are different types.
source: A key assumption of this framework is that neurons differing in axonal or dendritic patterns are different types.
evidence: Explicitly stated as a foundational assumption of the classification scheme.

claim: The same morphological pattern is further separated into distinct types if the neurons can be discriminated by neurotransmitter, synaptic selectivity, or consistent molecular and electrophysiological differences.
source: The same morphological pattern is further separated into distinct types if the neurons can be discriminated by neurotransmitter, synaptic selectivity, or consistent molecular and electrophysiological differences (see below), giving rise to 122 neuron types distinguished so far (18 in DG, 25 in CA3, 5 in CA2, 40 in CA1, 3 in Sub, and 31 in EC).
evidence: Stated as a criterion for neuron type classification with specific counts provided.

claim: Currently, 151 potential neuron types are placed 'on hold' until more data are published.
source: Currently, 151 potential neuron types are in this state (hippocampome.org/on-hold).
evidence: Stated as a count of neuron types with insufficient evidence for full inclusion.

claim: Hippocampal neurons mainly release glutamate or gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA).
source: Hippocampal neurons mainly release glutamate or gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) (Kullmann, 2007).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Putatively excitatory and inhibitory neurons in the hippocampus tend to have completely distinct morphologies.
source: Thus, putatively excitatory and inhibitory neurons in the hippocampus tend to have completely distinct morphologies.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the observation that only one case exists where neurons with the same axonal and dendritic patterns have different neurotransmitters.

claim: Only one case is known where neurons with the same axonal and dendritic patterns have different neurotransmitters: in CA1, Cajal–Retzius cells (glutamatergic) and Neurogliaform cells (GABAergic) both have axons and dendrites confined to SLM.
source: Interestingly, only one such case is known: in CA1, Cajal–Retzius cells, which were recently characterized as glutamatergic and more abundant than previously assumed in adult rats (Quattrocolo and Maccaferri, 2014), and (GABAergic) Neurogliaform cells (Price et al., 2005) have both axons and dendrites confined to SLM, though with extremely different arbor densities and shapes.
evidence: Stated with specific citations to supporting research.

claim: Most excitatory neurons in all hippocampal areas have long-range axons.
source: Although most excitatory neurons in all hippocampal areas have long-range axons, Hippocampome.org also includes several local glutamatergic types in DG, CA3, and CA1.
evidence: Stated as a general observation about excitatory neurons in the knowledge base.

claim: A substantial minority of GABAergic types in DG, CA3, and CA1 (16/71) have projecting axons.
source: Similarly, a substantial minority of GABAergic types in these areas (16/71) have projecting axons.
evidence: Stated with specific quantification from the knowledge base.

claim: Axo-axonic cells contact exclusively Pyramidal cells on the axon initial segments.
source: Axo-axonic cells, however, contact exclusively Pyramidal cells on the axon initial segments (Li et al., 1992; Ganter et al., 2004), whereas Basket cells synapse perisomatically on both principal neurons and interneurons (Buhl et al., 1994; Vida, 2010).
evidence: Stated with citation support for synaptic specificity.

claim: Basket cells synapse perisomatically on both principal neurons and interneurons.
source: Axo-axonic cells, however, contact exclusively Pyramidal cells on the axon initial segments (Li et al., 1992; Ganter et al., 2004), whereas Basket cells synapse perisomatically on both principal neurons and interneurons (Buhl et al., 1994; Vida, 2010).
evidence: Stated with citation support for synaptic specificity.

claim: The knowledge base has information on 96 biomarkers.
source: The knowledge base has information on 96 biomarkers, and positive or negative expression of at least one biomarker is known for two-thirds (81/122) of the neuron types (Figure 2; extended listing: hippocampome.org/markers).
evidence: Stated as a count of biomarkers in the knowledge base with reference to Figure 2.

claim: Positive or negative expression of at least one biomarker is known for two-thirds (81/122) of the neuron types.
source: The knowledge base has information on 96 biomarkers, and positive or negative expression of at least one biomarker is known for two-thirds (81/122) of the neuron types (Figure 2; extended listing: hippocampome.org/markers).
evidence: Stated as a quantification of biomarker coverage across neuron types.

claim: Parvalbumin (PV) is the most cited biomarker, appearing in ∼25% of the biomarker sources in Hippocampome.org.
source: The most cited biomarker is parvalbumin (PV), appearing in ∼25% of the biomarker sources in Hippocampome.org, and whose expression is known for 56 neuron types.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of biomarker citation frequency.

claim: Parvalbumin expression is known for 56 neuron types.
source: The most cited biomarker is parvalbumin (PV), appearing in ∼25% of the biomarker sources in Hippocampome.org, and whose expression is known for 56 neuron types.
evidence: Stated as a count of neuron types with known PV expression.

claim: Mossy cells express calretinin (CR) in mice, but not in rats.
source: For example, mossy cells express calretinin (CR) in mice (Blasco-Ibáñez and Freund, 1997), but not in rats (Freund et al., 1997).
evidence: Stated with citations showing species-specific differences in biomarker expression.

claim: In situ hybridization showed GABAA-α1 expression in rat CA1 Pyramidal cells, yet somatic immunohistochemistry of these neurons is negative; however, their dendrites show positive expression.
source: In another case, in situ hybridization showed GABAA-α1 expression in rat CA1 Pyramidal cells (Miralles et al., 1994), yet somatic immunohistochemistry of these neurons is negative; however, their dendrites show positive expression (Lopez-Tellez et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated with citations showing technique-specific and subcellular localization differences.

claim: CA3 Pyramidal cells are positive for chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor II (COUP-TFII) in the temporal, but not septal hippocampus.
source: For example, CA3 Pyramidal cells are positive for chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor II (COUP-TFII) in the temporal, but not septal hippocampus (Fuentealba et al., 2010).
evidence: Stated with citation showing location-specific biomarker expression.

claim: Superficial CA1 Pyramidal cells express calbindin (CB) while those deep in CA1 SP do not.
source: Similarly, superficial CA1 Pyramidal cells express calbindin (CB) while those deep in CA1 SP do not (Jinno et al., 1999; Sadowski et al., 2002).
evidence: Stated with citations showing depth-specific biomarker expression.

claim: Three-quarters of the neuron types (93/122) have measurements reported for four or more electrophysiological parameters.
source: Three-quarters of the neuron types (93/122) have measurements reported for four or more parameters, the most common being APampl, fast afterhyperpolarization amplitude (fAHP), and Vthresh.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of electrophysiological data coverage.

claim: The most common electrophysiological parameters measured are APampl, fast afterhyperpolarization amplitude (fAHP), and Vthresh.
source: Three-quarters of the neuron types (93/122) have measurements reported for four or more parameters, the most common being APampl, fast afterhyperpolarization amplitude (fAHP), and Vthresh.
evidence: Stated as an observation about the most frequently measured parameters.

claim: Hippocampome.org provides free, user-friendly online access to the entire information content.
source: Hippocampome.org provides free, user-friendly online access to the entire information content.
evidence: Stated as a description of the resource's accessibility.

claim: The annotated evidence supports 3697 distinct 'pieces of knowledge' (PoK).
source: The annotated evidence supports 3697 distinct 'pieces of knowledge' (PoK) regarding the presence or absence of axons or dendrites within any of the 26 parcels (e.g., Granule cells axons are found in CA3 SL represents one PoK), the expression or non-expression of a biomarker (e.g.,Granule cells are positive for CB), and individual electrophysiological properties (e.g., the APwidth of Granule cells is 1.71 ± 0.58 ms, mean ± standard deviation).
evidence: Stated as a quantification of the knowledge base content.

claim: The approximate ratio of morphological, molecular, and electrophysiological PoK is 5:3:2.
source: The approximate ratio of morphological, molecular, and electrophysiological PoK is 5:3:2.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of the distribution of knowledge types.

claim: CA1 is the most studied hippocampal area (1321 PoK).
source: While CA1 is the most studied hippocampal area (1321 PoK), outstanding knowledge gaps remain on interneuron diversity in subiculum (only Axo-axonic cells have enough information for inclusion as an active neuron type in Hippocampome.org) and EC (no GABAergic cells characterized with either soma or axons in deep layers).
evidence: Stated as a quantification of knowledge distribution across hippocampal areas.

claim: Outstanding knowledge gaps remain on interneuron diversity in subiculum (only Axo-axonic cells have enough information for inclusion as an active neuron type in Hippocampome.org).
source: While CA1 is the most studied hippocampal area (1321 PoK), outstanding knowledge gaps remain on interneuron diversity in subiculum (only Axo-axonic cells have enough information for inclusion as an active neuron type in Hippocampome.org) and EC (no GABAergic cells characterized with either soma or axons in deep layers).
evidence: Stated as an identification of knowledge gaps in the subiculum.

claim: Outstanding knowledge gaps remain in EC (no GABAergic cells characterized with either soma or axons in deep layers).
source: While CA1 is the most studied hippocampal area (1321 PoK), outstanding knowledge gaps remain on interneuron diversity in subiculum (only Axo-axonic cells have enough information for inclusion as an active neuron type in Hippocampome.org) and EC (no GABAergic cells characterized with either soma or axons in deep layers).
evidence: Stated as an identification of knowledge gaps in the entorhinal cortex.

claim: Hippocampome.org contains 13,888 pieces of evidence.
source: Hippocampome.org contains 13,888 pieces of evidence, including all known sources for many neuron types and properties, but only an adequate number of sources to firmly support established knowledge (e.g., we have only annotated a fraction of all published evidence that granule cells extend axons in CA3 SL).
evidence: Stated as a quantification of the evidence in the knowledge base.

claim: Positive or negative expression of neuropeptide Y (NPY) tends to co-occur, respectively, with high or low fAHP (p < 0.001 with Barnard's exact test; post hoc t-test p < 0.02 with real values from all n = 42 pieces of evidence).
source: for example, positive or negative expression of neuropeptide Y (NPY) tends to co-occur, respectively, with high or low fAHP (p < 0.001 with Barnard's exact test; post hoc t-test p < 0.02 with real values from all n = 42 pieces of evidence)
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis of the knowledge base data.

claim: Vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) is mutually exclusive with CB (p < 0.04).
source: vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) is mutually exclusive with CB (p < 0.04)
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis of the knowledge base data.

claim: Of 31 entorhinal neuron types, only Oblique Pyramidal cells in LII of medial EC have no layer overlap between axons and dendrites.
source: and of 31 entorhinal neuron types, only Oblique Pyramidal cells in LII of medial EC have no layer overlap between axons and dendrites.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the knowledge base data.

claim: CB is never co-expressed with either CR (p < 0.05, n = 19) or PV (NS, n = 31).
source: While CB is never co-expressed with either CR (p < 0.05, n = 19) or PV (NS, n = 31), PV and CR do co-occur in 2 out of 12 neuron types known to express at least one of them (p > 0.49, n = 31).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: PV and CR co-occur in 2 out of 12 neuron types known to express at least one of them (p > 0.49, n = 31).
source: While CB is never co-expressed with either CR (p < 0.05, n = 19) or PV (NS, n = 31), PV and CR do co-occur in 2 out of 12 neuron types known to express at least one of them (p > 0.49, n = 31).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Among the 24 neuron types for which the expression information on both CB and VIP is known, 14 are positive for either CB or VIP, but none express both (p < 0.04, n = 24).
source: A less known but more stringent relationship exists between CB and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP): among the 24 neuron types for which the expression information on both of these markers is known, 14 are positive for either CB or VIP, but none express both (p < 0.04, n = 24).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Clearly positive expression of NPY tends to coincide with very high values of fAHP (p < 0.001, n = 23) and Vthresh (p < 0.005, n = 21).
source: Clearly positive expression of neuropeptide Y (NPY) tends to coincide with very high values of the fast afterhyperpolarization (fAHP) (p < 0.001, n = 23) and membrane firing threshold (Vthresh) (p < 0.005, n = 21), and clearly negative expression tends to be associated with very low values of both parameters.
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: fAHP is related to expression of chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor II (CoupTF II) (p < 0.005, n = 14).
source: fAHP is similarly related also to expression of chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor II (CoupTF II) (p < 0.005, n = 14), which tends to clearly co-express either both positively or both negatively with NPY (p < 0.005, n = 18).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: CoupTF II tends to clearly co-express either both positively or both negatively with NPY (p < 0.005, n = 18).
source: fAHP is similarly related also to expression of chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor II (CoupTF II) (p < 0.005, n = 14), which tends to clearly co-express either both positively or both negatively with NPY (p < 0.005, n = 18).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Of 45 cell types with extreme values of input resistance (Rin) and membrane time constant (τm) (p < 0.001, n = 45), 43 are positively correlated (R2 = 0.70).
source: Confirming a well-known relationship, of 45 cell types with extreme values of input resistance (Rin) and membrane time constant (τm) (p < 0.001, n = 45), 43 are positively correlated (R2 = 0.70).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: High values of APwidth are associated with high values of Rin (p < 0.001, n = 45), and vice versa for the low values of both (R2 = 0.36).
source: Likewise, high values of the spike width (APwidth) are associated with high values of Rin (p < 0.001, n = 45), and vice versa for the low values of both (R2 = 0.36).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Of the 69 cell types with axons in more than one layer, only DG Granule and CA1 O-LMR do not have overlapping axons and dendrites (p < 0.001, n = 122).
source: Of the 69 cell types with axons in more than one layer, only DG Granule and CA1 O-LMR do not have overlapping axons and dendrites (p < 0.001, n = 122).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: All of the 43 cell types that have axons in three or more layers have axons that overlap with their dendrites (p < 0.001, n = 122).
source: All of the 43 cell types that have axons in three or more layers have axons that overlap with their dendrites (p < 0.001, n = 122).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Cell types with axons in three or more layers tend to have very high Rin (p < 0.001, n = 58) and τm (p < 0.001, n = 59).
source: Furthermore, cell types with axons in three or more layers tend to have very high Rin (p < 0.001, n = 58) and τm (p < 0.001, n = 59).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Clear expression of cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1) implies (in 5/5 cases) clear expression of cholecystokinin (CCK) (if known), and clear absence of CCK implies (in 8/8 cases) clear absence of CB1 (if known) (p < 0.005, n = 15).
source: Clear expression of cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1) implies (in 5/5 cases) clear expression of cholecystokinin (CCK) (if known), and clear absence of CCK implies (in 8/8 cases) clear absence of CB1 (if known) (p < 0.005, n = 15).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Independent of CCK expression, CB1 and VIP are not co-expressed in any of the eight types that are positive for either biomarker (NS, n = 17).
source: Of the two neuron types expressing CCK and not CB1, one expresses VIP; however, independent of CCK expression, CB1 and VIP are not co-expressed in any of the eight types that are positive for either biomarker (NS, n = 17).
evidence: Stated with statistical analysis in Box 1.

claim: Hippocampome.org contains known connectivity information for 202 out of 14,884 possible pairs (<2%) of neuron types.
source: Hippocampome.org contains known connectivity information (synapses or lack thereof, established e.g., by electron microscopy or paired electrophysiological recordings) among its neuron types. Such data, however, are only available for 202 out of 14,884 possible pairs (<2%).
evidence: Stated as a quantification of known connectivity data.

claim: The possibility of connections can be tentatively excluded for 11,668 pairs of neuron types (78.4%) based on non-overlapping distributions of their respective axons and dendrites.
source: The possibility of connections can be tentatively excluded for 11,668 pairs of neuron types (78.4%) based on non-overlapping distributions of their respective axons and dendrites.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of potential connectivity based on morphological data.

claim: In 3014 pairs (20%) the axons and dendrites of the two neuron types share at least one parcel.
source: In 3014 pairs (20%) the axons and dendrites of the two neuron types share at least one parcel.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of potential connectivity based on morphological overlap.

claim: Filled boxes along the main diagonal of the connectivity matrix, corresponding to neurons with axons and dendrites co-located in any parcel, indicate within-type connectivity (not necessarily autapses), and are more frequent among excitatory (87%) than inhibitory (67%) types.
source: Filled boxes along the main diagonal, corresponding to neurons with axons and dendrites co-located in any parcel (purple boxes in Figure 1F), indicate within-type connectivity (not necessarily autapses), and are more frequent among excitatory (87%) than inhibitory (67%) types.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 1F and quantification of within-type connectivity.

claim: All six areas of the hippocampal formation have potential excitatory connections to at least one other area.
source: Within the hippocampal formation, this relationship is illustrated explicitly in Figure 6B: all six areas have potential excitatory, and with the exception of Sub and EC, inhibitory connections to at least one other area, most of which are not considered in the canonical trisynaptic loop (cf. Burns and Young, 2000; van Strien et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 6B showing regional connectivity.

claim: All six areas of the hippocampal formation except Sub and EC have potential inhibitory connections to at least one other area.
source: Within the hippocampal formation, this relationship is illustrated explicitly in Figure 6B: all six areas have potential excitatory, and with the exception of Sub and EC, inhibitory connections to at least one other area, most of which are not considered in the canonical trisynaptic loop (cf. Burns and Young, 2000; van Strien et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 6B showing regional connectivity.

claim: The only potential monosynaptic connection between DG and CA1 is inhibitory.
source: The only potential monosynaptic connection between DG and CA1 is inhibitory.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the connectivity analysis.

claim: Granule cells can receive input from 26 neuron types (9 excitatory) across DG, CA3, CA1, and EC.
source: Granule cells can receive input from 26 neuron types (9 excitatory) across DG, CA3, CA1, and EC.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of potential inputs to Granule cells from Figure 7B.

claim: CA3 Basket cells can receive input from 31 types (8 excitatory), including Granule cells and other Basket cells.
source: CA3 Basket cells can receive input from 31 types (8 excitatory), including Granule cells and other Basket cells.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of potential inputs to CA3 Basket cells from Figure 7B.

claim: Granule cells potentially send output to 29 neuron types.
source: Granule cells potentially send output to 29 neuron types, counting all 13 that could receive information from CA3 Basket cells, including CA3 Basket cells themselves.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of potential outputs from Granule cells from Figure 7B.

claim: The distribution of axons and dendrites across anatomical areas and layers is known for the majority of hippocampal neurons identified to date and effectively discriminates among them.
source: The distribution of axons and dendrites across anatomical areas and layers is known for the majority of hippocampal neurons identified to date and effectively discriminates among them.
evidence: Stated as a justification for the classification approach.

claim: Morphology is considerably robust to experimental conditions among the features commonly used to describe cortical neurons.
source: Among the features commonly used to describe cortical neurons, morphology is also considerably robust to experimental conditions.
evidence: Stated as a justification for using morphology as a primary classification criterion.

claim: Axonal and dendritic patterns provide the blueprint for the potential network connectivity.
source: Furthermore, just like the positions of the elements in the Periodic Table indicate their potential to combine into molecules, axonal and dendritic patterns provide the blueprint for the potential network connectivity.
evidence: Stated as an analogy and justification for the classification approach.

claim: The resulting knowledge base constitutes the first comprehensive machine-readable neuron inventory for a mammalian cortical region.
source: The resulting knowledge base constitutes the first comprehensive machine-readable neuron inventory for a mammalian cortical region.
evidence: Stated as a claim about the uniqueness of the resource.

claim: Parallel efforts are underway for the retina, somatosensory and visual cortex, and drosophila.
source: Parallel efforts are underway for the retina (Siegert et al., 2009), somatosensory (Markram, 2006) and visual cortex (celltypes.brain-map.org), and drosophila (dos Santos et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citations to related efforts in other brain regions.

claim: The vision driving Hippocampome.org is a real-scale computer model of the entire hippocampal formation.
source: The vision driving Hippocampome.org is a real-scale computer model of the entire hippocampal formation.
evidence: Stated as the long-term goal of the project.

claim: Accurate simulations require knowledge of the component parts, their locations, numbers, properties, and connectivity.
source: Accurate simulations require knowledge of the component parts, their locations, numbers, properties, and connectivity.
evidence: Stated as a requirement for computational modeling.

claim: Further works-in-progress include neuron counts, firing patterns, synaptic profiles, developmental origins, and rhythmic phase-locking.
source: Further works-in-progress include neuron counts (Bezaire and Soltesz, 2013), firing patterns, synaptic profiles, developmental origins (Tricoire et al., 2011), and rhythmic phase-locking (Somogyi and Klausberger, 2005).
evidence: Stated as ongoing work to expand the knowledge base.

claim: The binary assignment of axonal and dendritic distribution across parcels will gradually be substituted by quantitative morphological estimates.
source: Moreover, the binary assignment of axonal and dendritic distribution across parcels will gradually be substituted by quantitative morphological estimates (Ropireddy and Ascoli, 2011).

claim: Neuronal classification will likely benefit by advances in optogenetics, sequencing, and machine learning.
source: Neuronal classification will likely benefit by advances in optogenetics, sequencing, and machine learning (Fenno et al., 2014; Kohara et al., 2014; Roux et al., 2014; Armañanzas and Ascoli, 2015; Zeisel et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as a prediction with citations to relevant technological advances.

claim: Rapid growth is expected particularly in the knowledge of molecular markers.
source: Rapid growth is expected particularly in the knowledge of molecular markers.
evidence: Stated as a prediction about future knowledge expansion.

claim: Thousands of the ∼20,000 genes mapped in the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas are expressed in the hippocampus.
source: Thousands of the ∼20,000 genes mapped in the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas (Lein et al., 2007) are expressed in the hippocampus.
evidence: Stated with citation to the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas.

claim: NeuroMorpho.Org, a digital archive of neuronal reconstructions, has enabled numerous secondary findings from amounts of data far outreaching the collection means of individual labs.
source: NeuroMorpho.Org (Ascoli et al., 2007), a digital archive of neuronal reconstructions, has enabled numerous secondary findings from amounts of data far outreaching the collection means of individual labs (Parekh and Ascoli, 2014).
evidence: Stated with citations as an example of the value of data integration.

claim: The limited interneuron diversity in CA3, CA2, Sub, and EC compared to CA1 suggests several to-be-discovered neurons.
source: The limited interneuron diversity in CA3, CA2, Sub, and EC compared to CA1 suggests several to-be-discovered neurons.

claim: Many cell types found in CA1 (e.g., Basket, O-LM, Ivy, Neurogliaform, Axo-axonic, Trilaminar, and Bistratified) have counterparts in some other area(s), but they are probably present in more.
source: Many cell types found in CA1 (e.g., Basket, O-LM, Ivy, Neurogliaform, Axo-axonic, Trilaminar, and Bistratified) have counterparts in some other area(s), but they are probably present in more.

claim: The Hippocampome.org framework sets a standard for the minimal information that must be included in publications describing hippocampal neuron types in order to link the resulting data to the existing body of knowledge.
source: The Hippocampome.org framework also sets a standard for the minimal information that must be included in publications describing hippocampal neuron types in order to link the resulting data to the existing body of knowledge.

claim: The germinal selection of information to include in Hippocampome.org was pragmatically guided by the density of available published data.
source: The germinal selection of information to include in Hippocampome.org was pragmatically guided by the density of available published data.

claim: In vivo neuronal reconstructions and recordings, although extremely valuable, are too sparse to be adopted as defining dimensions in a comprehensive census of neuron types.
source: For example, in vivo neuronal reconstructions and recordings, although extremely valuable, are too sparse to be adopted as defining dimensions in a comprehensive census of neuron types.

claim: Axonal and dendritic patterns are more commonly identified across layers than in the longitudinal (septo-temporal) and transverse (e.g., CA3a,b,c) axes.
source: Similarly, axonal and dendritic patterns are more commonly identified across layers than in the longitudinal (septo-temporal) and transverse (e.g., CA3a,b,c) axes.

claim: CA3c Pyramidal cells are differentiated from other CA3 Pyramidal cells, because of their axonal back-projection to DG and lack of dendrites in SLM.
source: For instance, CA3c Pyramidal cells are differentiated from other CA3 Pyramidal cells, because of their axonal back-projection to DG and lack of dendrites in SLM.

source: Some neuron types are similarly separated between medial and lateral EC.
evidence: Stated as an example of finer anatomical distinctions.

claim: Hippocampome.org infrastructure is designed to accommodate additions along many dimensions: new areas (e.g., septum), finer parcels (medial vs lateral EC), additional neuron types, and graded reporting of neurite densities.
source: Moreover, Hippocampome.org infrastructure is designed to accommodate additions along many dimensions: new areas (e.g., septum), finer parcels (medial vs lateral EC), additional neuron types (hippocampome.org/future), and graded reporting of neurite densities.
evidence: Stated as a description of the resource's extensibility.

claim: The open-source code of this resource encourages community-led extension to other brain regions, inter-operability with related initiatives, and progressive adoption of unique identifiers for neuron types and properties.
source: The open-source code of this resource also encourages community-led extension to other brain regions, inter-operability with related initiatives, and progressive adoption of unique identifiers for neuron types and properties.
evidence: Stated as a description of the resource's open-source nature and goals.

claim: A neuron type must satisfy four criteria to be included in Hippocampome.org: (1) The soma must be located in the hippocampal formation. (2) The major neurotransmitter must be at least tentatively specifiable. (3) The locations of both axons and dendrites within any of the 26 hippocampal parcels must be clearly presented. (4) Experimental evidence of more than a single neuron of the type must be reported.
source: A neuron type must satisfy four criteria to be included in Hippocampome.org. (1) The soma must be located in the hippocampal formation. (2) The major neurotransmitter must be at least tentatively specifiable; at present, only glutamatergic and GABAergic types have qualified for inclusion in Hippocampome.org (see below for cholinergic). (3) The locations of both axons and dendrites within any of the 26 hippocampal parcels (Figure 1A,B) must be clearly presented, either textually or graphically. (4) Experimental evidence of more than a single neuron of the type must be reported.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as inclusion criteria.

claim: All evidence collated in Hippocampome.org comes from peer-reviewed articles or book chapters and pertains to healthy rodents, predominantly rats and mice ≥13 days old.
source: All evidence collated in Hippocampome.org comes from peer-reviewed articles or book chapters (hippocampome.org/bibliography) and pertains to healthy rodents, predominantly rats and mice ≥13 days old.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as data inclusion criteria.

claim: For neuronal reconstructions and schematics, a layer must contain either ≥15% of the overall arbor or at least half the amount included in the most abundant layer, and the neurite must penetrate ≥15% of the layer depth.
source: For neuronal reconstructions and schematics, a layer must contain either ≥15% of the overall arbor or at least half the amount included in the most abundant layer. Moreover, the neurite must penetrate ≥15% of the layer depth.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as encoding thresholds.

claim: The term 'most' referring to branches is considered as evidence for presence within that parcel, while the term 'some' is not.
source: The term 'most' referring to branches is considered as evidence for presence within that parcel, while the term 'some' is not, although the quote is still included in Hippocampome.org as evidential information.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as an interpretive rule.

claim: If the number of neurons in each subset is greater than the square root of the total number of neurons described, differing axonal and dendritic patterns lead to multiple Hippocampome neuron types.
source: This occurs if the number of neurons in each subset is greater than the square root of the total number of neurons described (e.g., if 4 neurons out of 15 have distinct neurite distributions, they would be split into a different cell type because 4 > √15).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a rule for splitting neuron types.

claim: DG neurogliaform cells are divided into two separate neuron types: those that extend their axons into Sub (keeping the name 'DG Neurogliaform') and those that remain local within DG SMo, which are merged with MOPP cells.
source: For instance, DG neurogliaform cells (Armstrong et al., 2011) are divided into two separate neuron types: those that extend their axons into Sub (keeping the name 'DG Neurogliaform') and those that remain local within DG SMo. This latter type is merged with MOPP cells, which have the same axo-dendritic pattern in DG and no projection.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as an example of neuron type splitting and merging.

claim: R-LM and P-LM cells, differing only in somatic location, are merged into a single CA1 OR-LM type in Hippocampome.org.
source: Conversely, neurons assigned to different groups in a paper might belong to the same Hippocampome type, such as R-LM and P-LM cells (Oliva et al., 2000), that differing only in somatic location, are merged into a single CA1 OR-LM type in Hippocampome.org.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as an example of neuron type merging.

claim: Hippocampome.org neuron names are assigned a prefix denoting their hippocampal area if the same name is used for neurons in different areas, but not if the name is unique.
source: Common neuron names in Hippocampome.org are assigned a prefix denoting their hippocampal area if the same name is used for neurons in different areas (e.g., CA3 Bistratified and CA1 Bistratified), but not if the name is unique (as in the case of HIPP cells, which only exist in DG).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a naming convention.

claim: The prefix MEC is assigned to neurons that have been characterized solely (or are known to exist predominantly) in the medial EC.
source: Furthermore, the prefix MEC is assigned to neurons that have been characterized solely (or are known to exist predominantly) in the medial EC, such as MEC Layer II Stellate cells.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a naming convention.

claim: The prefix LEC is assigned to lateral entorhinal neurons.
source: Similarly, the prefix LEC is assigned to lateral entorhinal neurons.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a naming convention.

claim: Neurons that are believed to exist in both the medial and lateral ECs are generically referred to with the prefix EC.
source: In contrast, neurons that are believed to exist in both the medial and lateral ECs are generically referred to with the prefix EC.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a naming convention.

claim: To search for molecular and electrophysiological data, the articles defining the axonal–dendritic pattern of each Hippocampome.org neuron type are mined first, followed by all references citing or cited by these sources, and lastly full-text searches using all known synonyms.
source: To search for molecular and electrophysiological data, the articles defining the axonal–dendritic pattern of each Hippocampome.org neuron type are mined first. All references citing (webofknowledge.com) or cited by these sources are mined next. Lastly, full-text searches using all known synonyms of the target property and neuron type are performed (scholar.google.com and previously scirus.com).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as the literature search strategy.

claim: For inclusion in the knowledge base, molecular and electrophysiological data must be linked to a morphologically defined neuron type.
source: For inclusion in the knowledge base, molecular and electrophysiological data must be linked to a morphologically defined neuron type.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a linking requirement.

claim: Principal cells within their layers (i.e., granule cells in DG and pyramidal cells in CA1 SP) can be identified as positive or negative for a biomarker because the layers are >90% homogeneous for the principal cells and the somata are densely packed.
source: The first applies to principal cells within their layers (i.e., granule cells in DG and pyramidal cells in CA1 SP). These neuron types are readily identified as positive or negative for a biomarker because the layers are >90% homogeneous for the principal cells (Czéh et al., 2013) and the somata are densely packed.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a linking exception with citation.

claim: Certain groups of neurons can be identified by their axonal tracts, for example, granule cells by their mossy fibers and medial EC LII stellate cells by their perforant path projection.
source: In the second case, certain groups of neurons can be identified by their axonal tracts, for example, granule cells by their mossy fibers and medial EC LII stellate cells by their perforant path projection.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a linking exception.

claim: The 20 most studied biomarkers in hippocampal research include calcium-binding proteins (PV, CB, CR), receptors and transporters (CB1, sub P rec, muscarinic receptor 2, serotonin receptor 3, vesicular glutamate transporter 3, metabotropic glutamate receptor 1α, GABAA-α1 subunit), neuropeptides (CCK, SOM, enkephalin, NPY, VIP, neurogranin), and a miscellaneous group of cytoskeletal and extracellular matrix proteins (α-actinin 2, reelin), transcription factors (COUP-TFII), and enzymes (nNOS).
source: The 20 most studied biomarkers in hippocampal research (Figure 2; extended listing: hippocampome.org/markers) were targeted for literature searches across all 122 neuron types. These include calcium-binding proteins (PV, CB, CR), receptors and transporters (CB1, sub P rec, muscarinic receptor 2, serotonin receptor 3, vesicular glutamate transporter 3, metabotropic glutamate receptor 1α, GABAA-α1 subunit), neuropeptides (CCK, SOM, enkephalin, NPY, VIP, neurogranin), and a miscellaneous group of cytoskeletal and extracellular matrix proteins (α-actinin 2, reelin), transcription factors (COUP-TFII), and enzymes (nNOS).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as the biomarkers targeted for literature searches.

claim: When a single population of neurons is shown to be divisible into clearly negative and clearly positive subpopulations for a biomarker, this is taken as an indication of biomarker subtypes.
source: When a single population of neurons is shown to be divisible into clearly negative and clearly positive subpopulations, this is taken as an indication of biomarker subtypes.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as an interpretive rule for biomarker expression.

claim: The knowledge base includes passive (Rin, τm, resting membrane potential or Vrest), spike (APampl, APwidth, Vthresh, fAHP), and other response parameters (maxFR, sAHP, hyperpolarization sag ratio).
source: The knowledge base includes passive (Rin, τm, resting membrane potential or Vrest), spike (APampl, APwidth, Vthresh, fAHP), and other response parameters (maxFR, sAHP, hyperpolarization sag ratio).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as the electrophysiological parameters included.

source: Although these properties can be defined and measured in multiple ways, Hippocampome.org standardizes the data according to a single definition (hippocampome.org/ephys-defs).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as a data standardization approach.

source: The growth, evolution, and accuracy of Hippocampone.org content rely on two main mechanisms: continuous literature mining (hippocampome.org/ongoing-mining) and community feedback (hippocampome.org/feedback).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as the maintenance strategy.

source: We update the bibliographic listing at quarterly intervals (based on citation alerts for many of the core review articles as well as perusals of new issues of most mainline neuroscience publications), adding new relevant references and linking to the knowledge base the articles that have been annotated.
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as the update schedule.

claim: Pairwise correlations were explored between 205 properties of Hippocampome neuron types using 2 × 2 contingency matrices with Barnard's exact test.
source: We explored pairwise correlations between 205 properties of Hippocampome neuron types, including neurotransmitter; axonal, dendritic, and somatic locations in the 26 partitions and 6 areas; the projecting (inter-areas) or local (intra-area) nature of axons and dendrites; axon and dendrite co-presence within any partition; axonal and dendritic presence in a single layer only or in ≥3 layers; clear positive or negative expression of any biomarkers; and high (top third) or low (bottom third) values for seven electrophysiological properties (excluding highly stimulus-dependent sag ratio, sAHP, and maxFR). To evaluate the correlations between these categorical properties, we use 2 × 2 contingency matrices with Barnard's exact test, which provides the greatest statistical power when row and column totals are free to vary (Lydersen et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated in the Materials and methods as the statistical analysis approach.

claim: Barnard's exact test provides the greatest statistical power when row and column totals are free to vary.
source: To evaluate the correlations between these categorical properties, we use 2 × 2 contingency matrices with Barnard's exact test, which provides the greatest statistical power when row and column totals are free to vary (Lydersen et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with citation as justification for the statistical test used.
